## Course Description

ECO 112 introduces you to macroeconomics: the study of modern economies at a national level. We'll focus on national income accounts, monetary and fiscal policy, and economic growth, building toward the ability to analyze national economies, engage in policy debates, and follow international economic events.

## Textbook

- [McConnell, Brue, and Flynn: *Macroeconomics*, 2026 Release](https://www.mheducation.com/), McGraw Hill Education

The electronic edition is **required** through McGraw Hill Connect (which also hosts homework, quizzes, and SmartBook readings); a print copy is optional.

## How the Course Runs

- **Tuesday:** Homework/quiz due on the previous chapter, then lecture on a new chapter.
- **Thursday:** Student presentation on the previous chapter (starting Week 6), then lecture continues.


## Grading

| Category | % of Grade |
|---|---|
| Exam 1 | 25% |
| Exam 2 | 25% |
| Presentation | 20% |
| Connect Homework | 20% |
| Quizzes | 10% |

Quizzes are short, paper, in-class checks of understanding (two lowest dropped). Homework is completed on Connect, due Tuesdays. Presentations start in Week 6 and run through 7 slots across the semester.

Full policy detail, including the late-work policy, AI use policy, attendance requirements, and university-required statements, is in the official syllabus below.

## Assignments

Homework is completed in Connect, tied to each chapter. See the [Schedule](index.qmd) page for exact due dates.
